title: Kenyan Mango Kachumbari
community: Popular across Kenya — especially popular in summer
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kachumbari ya Embe — Mango Kachumbari. The beloved classic kachumbari elevated with diced ripe mango — adding tropical sweetness to the sharp, fresh salad. The perfect condiment for grilled fish and coastal dishes.
longDesc: Mango kachumbari takes Kenya's most beloved condiment and adds the country's most celebrated tropical fruit. The mango's sweetness perfectly balances the sharpness of the onion and lemon, creating a condiment that is simultaneously refreshing, fruity, and bright. It is especially popular alongside grilled fish and coastal seafood dishes.
ingredients: 1 large ripe mango — peeled and finely diced
1 medium onion — finely diced and rinsed in cold water
steps: Rinse diced onion in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain — this removes harshness.
Combine mango, tomatoes, drained onion, chilli, and coriander in a bowl.
Add lime juice, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Taste and adjust — more lime for tartness, more mango for sweetness.
chefTips: Rinsing the onion in cold water removes the sharp harshness while keeping the crunch.
Use a mango that is ripe but still firm — it should hold its shape when diced.
The combination of lime and lemon adds complexity that either alone does not provide.
commonMistakes: Overripe, mushy mango — the salsa becomes watery.
Not rinsing the onion — too aggressive and sharp.
cookingScience: Rinsing raw onion in cold water dissolves the sulphur compounds responsible for eye-watering sharpness. The compounds are water-soluble and leach out in 5 minutes of soaking — the onion retains its texture and crunch but loses its harsh edge.
sustainabilityTips: Make during mango season when mangoes are most abundant and affordable.
storage: Best eaten within 2 hours — the mango releases juice over time.
healthBenefits: Mango is rich in vitamins A and C.
culturalNote: Mango kachumbari is the celebration upgrade of Kenya's most beloved condiment — served at coastal restaurants, holiday gatherings, and any occasion when the finest Kenyan mangoes are in season.
